---
title: "TAF readiness level"
---

The TAF readiness level (TRL) says how far a stock assessment has come towards being a quality assured, published TAF assessment. There are four levels.

| Level | Reached when |
|---|---|
| 1 | The assessment code is on GitHub. |
| 2 | The code passes the QC test. |
| 3 | The code passes the QC run test. |
| 4 | The assessment is published and linked to advice. |

The levels build on each other. An assessment can only reach level 2 after reaching level 1, level 3 after level 2, and level 4 after level 3.

## The levels

### Level 1: code on GitHub

The assessment has a repository in the [ices-taf](https://github.com/ices-taf) organisation containing its code. This is checked by looking for model scripts in the repository, `model.R`, any scripts named `model_*.R` and any R Markdown files named `model*.Rmd`, with more in them than the empty `model.R` a new TAF repository starts with.

### Level 2: passes the QC test

The code passes the automated quality checks. This is the validation step in the [process workflow](process-workflow.qmd). The results for each repository are published by the [QC dashboard](https://github.com/ices-tools-prod/taf-qc-dashboard).

An assessment passes when all the checks pass. It also passes when it fails only because it has no `SOFTWARE.bib` file, that is when the two checks `qc.software.bib.exists` and `qc.software.bib.valid` are the only ones to fail. A `SOFTWARE.bib` file that is present but not valid is a failure.

### Level 3: passes the QC run test

The code runs successfully from start to finish. This is the execution step in the [process workflow](process-workflow.qmd).

### Level 4: published and linked to advice

The assessment is published in the [ices-advice](https://github.com/ices-advice) organisation and linked from the advice for the stock.

## Current status

- Levels 1 and 2 are in use. The number of assessments at each level is shown under [TAF readiness](../status/readiness.qmd).
- Level 3 is under development, so no stock has reached it.
- Published assessments are recorded alongside their level. An assessment only counts as level 4 once it has also passed levels 2 and 3, so none is at level 4 yet.

The software behind the checks is described under [software components](components.qmd).
